description: REQ-106's own iteration-3 fix for FIND-103 (the crash-safe two-phase provisional/follow-up ledger record) does NOT actually close the double-disbursement gap for a distinct, equally realistic failure mode: an IN-PROCESS (non-crash) exception thrown from `payViaFacilitator` AFTER the facilitator's own `/settle` call has ALREADY succeeded (i.e., the transfer has already been broadcast/executed). Re-read this session, `escrow.mjs::settleBody` (lines 124-140) has ZERO try/catch around its own `await publicClient.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash: tx })` call (line 135) -- this call happens strictly AFTER `/settle` already returned `success:true` (line 129-132), meaning the real on-chain transfer has already been submitted. `waitForTransactionReceipt` can genuinely throw (RPC timeout/network error/receipt-not-found-within-polling-window) in this exact window, and when it does, the exception propagates UNCAUGHT out of `settleBody` and out of `payViaFacilitator` (neither function has a try/catch around this call). Because REQ-106's own Acceptance Criteria specifies that the ENTIRE loan-issuance critical section -- including the disbursement call and the ledger append -- runs INSIDE the single `fn()` callback passed to `withGigLock(LOANS_LEDGER_PATH, loan_${lenderId}, fn)` (line 727-729), an uncaught exception from `payViaFacilitator` propagates all the way out of `fn()` without ever reaching REQ-106's own step 3 (`appendChild` the follow-up row). Re-read this session, `lock.mjs::withGigLock` (lines 187-209) wraps `fn()` in a plain `try { return await fn(); } finally { clearInterval(heartbeat); await release(statePath, lockKey); }` (lines 203-208) -- when `fn()` throws, this `finally` block releases the per-lender lock CLEANLY via `fs.unlink` (a NORMAL release, not a stale-lock timeout). REQ-106's own text scopes `reconcileProvisionalDisbursement` (the on-chain lookup that is supposed to recover a crashed attempt's real transfer) EXCLUSIVELY to 'a caller that reclaims a stale loan_${lenderId} lock' (lines 668-672) -- never to 'a caller that acquires an already-cleanly-released lock via the normal fast path.' Because the lock in this scenario is released cleanly (not left stale), the NEXT caller for this SAME lender takes `lock.mjs`'s normal `tryCreateLockFile` fast path (line 156), NOT the stale-reclaim path (line 157/128-151) -- so `reconcileProvisionalDisbursement` is NEVER invoked for this scenario at all, despite `nextLoanSequenceForLender` (per its own spec, lines 665-668) still treating the highest `n`'s `'provisioning'` row as claimed with no terminal follow-up. REQ-106's own edge-case enumeration only covers (a) 'crashes mid-issuance, BEFORE payViaFacilitator is even attempted' (lines 700-705, safe: no transfer occurred) and (b) 'crashes mid-issuance AFTER payViaFacilitator's own on-chain settle SUCCEEDS but BEFORE the follow-up row is appended' framed EXCLUSIVELY as a PROCESS CRASH requiring stale-lock reclaim (lines 706-715) -- it never enumerates 'the SAME process, still alive, catches (or fails to catch) an exception from payViaFacilitator thrown after /settle already succeeded, and the lock is released normally.' The spec's own disbursement-failure paragraph ('IF that call fails for ANY reason... THE SYSTEM SHALL fail closed... the FOLLOW-UP row is appended with status: disbursement_failed... this specific n is terminally closed', lines 683-692) treats every failure identically (append disbursement_failed, open n+1) -- but doing so for THIS specific failure mode (settle already succeeded, only the receipt-wait threw) risks either (i) permanently orphaning a REAL transfer that has already moved real money out of the lender's wallet while marking it 'disbursement_failed' and immediately allowing a SECOND real disbursement at n+1 for the SAME borrower request (an actual double-disbursement), or (ii) an implementer, following the letter of the spec, wrapping this in a try/catch that swallows the exception and mislabels an actually-successful (or ambiguous) transfer as failed. Either way, this is the SAME double-disbursement/untracked-transfer hazard FIND-103 was supposed to close, reintroduced via a code path the fix's own reconciliation logic is never wired to reach.

evidence.snippet: 1. IMMEDIATELY after computing n = nextLoanSequenceForLender(...) ... THE SYSTEM SHALL appendChild a PROVISIONAL row ... 2. THE SYSTEM SHALL THEN attempt the disbursement transfer (payViaFacilitator). 3. THE SYSTEM SHALL THEN appendChild a FOLLOW-UP row ... a caller that reclaims a stale loan_${lenderId} lock ... SHALL, BEFORE deciding to retry or mark the attempt failed, perform a REAL on-chain lookup ...

crossCheck.note: settleBody() has no try/catch around `await publicClient.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash: tx })` (line 135), which runs strictly AFTER `/settle` already returned success (lines 129-132) -- an exception here (timeout/RPC error) propagates uncaught out of payViaFacilitator despite the underlying transfer already having been submitted. Cross-referenced against /Users/anicca/anicca/skills/economy/gig/lib/lock.mjs lines 187-209 (withGigLock's try/finally releases the lock NORMALLY, via fs.unlink, on any thrown exception from fn() -- never leaving it 'stale' for the reclaim path that REQ-106's own reconcileProvisionalDisbursement text is exclusively scoped to).
